title: Archiving Plaques: Saving Virus Purification for Later
author: Kathryn Kauffman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j77crrn

steps.title: Mark plaques on dish
steps.instruction: Write a unique number next to each plaque on the bottom of the petri dish; if handling hundreds of plaques, split cataloging and archiving over three consecutive days as suggested.

steps.title: Log plaque properties
steps.instruction: Enter plaque details (e.g., detection day, size, appearance) for each numbered plaque into the archival spreadsheet provided.

steps.title: Prepare 96‑well storage plate
steps.instruction: Aliquot 250 µL of host growth media (or chosen buffer) into 48 alternating wells of a 96‑well plate to minimize cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Collect plaque plugs
steps.instruction: For each plaque, use a 1 mL pipette tip held by hand to bore through the plaque to the dish bottom, twist to sever the agar plug, pull the tip free, insert its delivery end into the designated well, and press the tip opening with a finger to expel the plug into the media (repeat presses if needed). After all plugs are harvested, seal the plate with a sterile adhesive aluminum cover and store at 4 °C overnight to allow virions to elute.

substeps.instruction: Hold 1 mL pipette tip and bore through plaque to bottom of dish.
Twist tip to fully sever the agar plug.
Pull tip free, insert delivery end into the assigned well.
Press top of tip to expel plug into 250 µL media; repeat as needed.
Confirm plug is in the media.
Seal plate with sterile adhesive aluminum cover.

steps.title: Prepare filter‑bottom plate
steps.instruction: Remove a filter‑bottom plate from its package, place it snugly on a receiver plate, and if using centrifugal filtration, seal the two plates together with laboratory tape.

steps.title: Transfer eluates to filter plate
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, transfer 125 µL from each well of the overnight storage plate to the corresponding well of the filter‑bottom plate (the presence of a small agar fragment in the tip does not affect the eluate).

steps.title: Filter plug eluate
steps.instruction: Filter the transferred eluate either by vacuum filtration with a vacuum manifold or by centrifugal filtration: spin the plate for up to 30 minutes at ≤5,000 rcf (maximum speed) to collect the filtrate.

substeps.instruction: Vacuum filtration using a vacuum manifold.
Centrifugal filtration: spin ≤5,000 rcf for ≤30 min.

steps.title: Store cell‑free stock at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Discard the filter‑bottom plate, cover the receiver plate with a sterile adhesive aluminum foil cover, and keep the filtrate (cell‑free virus) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Store frozen stock with glycerol
steps.instruction: Add 125 µL of 50 % glycerol solution to the remaining 125 µL in the original plaque‑eluate plate and store the mixture at –20 °C or –80 °C to prevent cell growth.

steps.title: Recover plaques for experiments
steps.instruction: Use the Tube‑free Agar Overlay or Molten Streaking for Singles protocols to prepare fresh plaque plates from the archived eluates as needed.
